prompt.context: Our client is Medvision, an X-ray equipment manufacturer. Its products are currently 98% analog and 2% digital, both of which are sold directly by sales force. The client's European division is suffering from declining profit.
prompt.question: The client has brought us in to find why its profits are declining and what to do about it.

clarifying_info.q: What is the market environment like?
clarifying_info.a: There is price pressure by buyers (hospitals) to control costs.

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue streams for Medvision?
Can you provide film pricing and volume data over time?
clarifying_info.a: 1999 price: 6.67; 2003 price: 5.00; 1999 volume: 300M; 2003 volume: 500M; 1999 revenue: 2000M; 2003 revenue: 2500M.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any issues with the sales force?
clarifying_info.a: Some salespeople give more discounts to clients than others.
Costs were already cut to the bones.

framework: Identify all revenue streams (machines, films, service) and assess which is most significant
Analyze revenue trends over time — focus on price vs. volume changes in largest segment (films)
Investigate cost structure — determine whether cost increases or revenue decline drives profit pressure
Examine sales force behavior — assess consistency of discount practices across sales reps
Identify controllable vs. uncontrollable drivers and prioritize recommendations

questions.prompt: What are the three revenue streams and which should be the focus of analysis?
questions.guidance: Machine/equipment: 800M; Films: 2500M (largest, ~74% of revenue); Service: 100M. Films is the most significant revenue stream and should be examined first for profit decline drivers.

math.answer: Films account for ~74% of revenue and is the primary focus.

questions.prompt: How has the films business changed between 1999 and 2003? What drove the revenue change?
questions.guidance: Revenue grew from 2000M to 2500M (+25%), but this was driven entirely by volume growth. Price declined significantly from 6.67 to 5.00, a 25% decrease in 4 years. Despite a ~67% volume increase (300M to 500M units), margin is being squeezed by price erosion driven by hospital buyer pressure.

math.setup: Price change: (5.00 - 6.67) / 6.67; Volume change: (500 - 300) / 300; Revenue check: price × volume each year
steps: Despite 67% volume growth, revenue only grew 25% because price fell 25%
math.answer: Price declined ~25% over 4 years; volume grew ~67%; revenue grew only ~25%. Profit declined because price erosion outpaced volume gains.

questions.prompt: The interviewer pulls out a table showing sales revenue and discounts by salesperson. What does this reveal?
questions.guidance: Some salespeople are giving far more discounts than others. This inconsistency in discount practices directly reduces realized prices below list price and further erodes profit margins. This is a controllable internal driver as opposed to external hospital buyer pressure.

brainstorming.prompt: What should Medvision do to address its declining profitability?

categories.name: Sales force management
ideas: Revise commission structure to align salesperson incentives with company profit (e.g., commission on margin rather than revenue)
Set maximum allowable discount thresholds by tier or product
Implement discount approval process for discounts above a set level
Train sales reps on value-based selling to reduce reliance on price discounts

categories.name: Pricing strategy
ideas: Implement standardized pricing floors to prevent excessive discounting
Bundle films with service contracts to protect realized price
Move toward value-based pricing tied to clinical outcomes
Introduce tiered pricing by hospital size or volume

categories.name: Revenue mix
ideas: Accelerate shift to digital products which may carry better margins
Explore long-term supply contracts with hospitals to lock in volume at better prices

categories.name: Cost and operations
ideas: Although costs are already cut, explore supply chain efficiencies in film production
Consider outsourcing lower-margin analog film production

recommendation: The primary driver of declining profit in Medvision's European division is price erosion in the films segment, where price fell ~25% from 1999 to 2003 due to hospital buyer pressure
A controllable internal contributor is inconsistent sales force discounting, which further reduces realized prices below what is necessary
Medvision should immediately restructure its sales commission model to tie compensation to margin rather than revenue, and establish maximum discount guardrails
risks: Hospital buyers may continue to exert downward pricing pressure regardless of internal sales force fixes
Overly restrictive discount policies could cause Medvision to lose volume to competitors
Digital transition may cannibalize analog film revenue faster than expected
next_steps: Audit full discount data by salesperson across all European markets to quantify revenue leakage
Design and pilot a margin-based commission structure with a subset of the sales force
Assess competitive pricing landscape to determine defensible price floors
Evaluate digital product roadmap and timeline for increasing the 2% digital share
